Carpet 3.3.1

  • Fixed: the footer on a saved text note (source + time) could occasionally render upside-down in the library. Notes now display as lightweight text and only load the full editor when you click to edit — so the layout can't flip, and there are fewer heavy editors in memory.

Carpet 3.3.0 — stability & memory

A reliability-focused release that tackles the high-RAM and occasional-crash reports.

  • Lower memory use. Screenshots and previews are now decoded at a downsampled size (OCR, thumbnails, link images), and image work happens off the main thread — so big captures no longer spike RAM or stall the UI.
  • Survives a damaged library. If the data file is corrupted (e.g. after a hard shutdown), Carpet now recovers and keeps running instead of failing to launch. Your saved files on disk are safe.
  • Leaner under load. The library grid renders on demand as you scroll, the search index has a memory ceiling, and network fetches are size-capped.
  • Grid fixes. Switching filters now re-balances the layout correctly, and cards no longer overlap.

A bigger, Spotlight-style search

  • Larger search bar. "Ask your Memory" is now a big, Spotlight-sized field — easier to read and faster to type into.
  • Bigger Open App button. The notch's Open App shortcut is larger and easier to hit.
  • Smaller fake notch on external monitors. On displays without a real notch, the simulated notch is more compact and sits flush in the menu bar.

Search inside your documents

  • Documents are now searchable by their contents. Carpet reads the text out of PDFs, Word, RTF, plain text and code files, so a search matches what's inside a file, not just its name.
  • New Documents tab. Saved files are sorted by kind — images join the photo grid, audio and video go to Music and Videos, and everything else lands in a dedicated Documents tab instead of Links.
  • Tidier notch. The recents strip is centered with balanced spacing, and Open App now sits neatly on the right.
